note: Each benchmark was run by a fresh headless Claude Code session that received only the /investigate prompt, a one-paragraph description of the behaviour and the glassbox MCP tools: no file access, no web, no shell, no hints about the mechanism. Blind here means exactly that and no more. The scientist is Claude, which has very likely seen these published results in training, so this is not evidence of discovery from zero knowledge. What it does show is that every claim in each report is backed by an experiment that ran in that session (the report tool refuses claims without evidence ids), and how many experiments and minutes that took. This file with the ground truth was written after the three runs had finished.

modadd.title: Modular addition (1-layer transformer, mod 113)
modadd.ground_truth: Nanda, Chan, Lieberum, Smith, Steinhardt (2023), Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability. The model here was trained from scratch for this repo (benchmarks/modadd/model/training.json), so the key frequencies are specific to this training run.

items.item: Inputs are embedded as sines and cosines at a sparse set of key frequencies
items.comment: Top frequencies 28, 17, 2, 14 (plus 27); 9 frequencies hold 92% of embedding power.

items.item: Attention moves a and b to the '=' position
items.comment: All 4 heads attend about 50/50 to a and b; jointly ablating them removes the behaviour.

items.item: The MLP combines the two operands into cos/sin of w(a+b) using products (trig identities)
items.comment: Found: MLP is necessary, neurons are tuned to single key frequencies, MLP output is periodic in the key frequencies. Not shown: the product terms themselves. The run's own test of this step (a probe) failed to execute and it said so.

items.item: The unembedding reads the answer out as sum over key frequencies of cos(w(a+b-c))
items.comment: Found: W_U uses the same frequencies, and removing that 12-dim subspace at the output removes the behaviour. The cos(w(a+b-c)) form appears in the pseudocode but was not measured directly on the logits.

items.item: The key frequencies are causally necessary and sufficient
items.comment: 18 of 128 embedding dims: removed -> 0.9% accuracy; kept alone -> 100%; random 18 dims removed -> 100%.

induction.title: Induction (2-layer attention-only model)
induction.ground_truth: Elhage, Nanda, Olsson et al. (2021), A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits. The paper describes the mechanism; it does not give head indices for this particular checkpoint (TransformerLens 'attn-only-2l'), so the rubric is at mechanism level.
induction.report_status: partial / not verified · partial: causal checks pass at full precision, agreement check fails

items.comment: Head 0.3: 0.53 of attention on the previous position; ablating it costs 8.8 nats.

items.item: A layer-1 induction head that attends to the token after the earlier occurrence of the current token
items.comment: Head 1.6: 0.64 attention to that token; shown to be content-based by changing the repeat length.

items.item: K-composition: the previous-token head feeds the induction head's keys
items.comment: Path 0.3 -> 1.6 key restores 0.77; the value path restores about 0.

items.item: The induction head's OV circuit copies the attended token to the output
items.comment: 1.6 writes 81% of the logit difference directly.

items.item: The written-out algorithm predicts the model on held-out inputs
items.comment: Causal checks pass, but agreement is 0.605 because the model is only 60% accurate on this task. V0002 used only 10 held-out inputs.

ioi.title: Indirect object identification (GPT-2 small)
ioi.ground_truth: Wang, Variengien, Conmy, Shlegeris, Steinhardt (2022), Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small. Head lists below are the 26 heads of the published circuit.
ioi.report_status: partial / not verified · verified (local-full, full precision)

items.item: Name mover heads attend from the last token to the indirect object and copy it
Negative name mover heads write against the answer
S-inhibition heads read the repeated subject and steer the name movers' queries
items.comment: 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10 via path patching into name-mover queries.

items.item: Induction and duplicate-token heads detect the repeated name
items.comment: Induction 4 of 4; duplicate token 2 of 3 (0.10 missed).

items.item: Previous-token heads feed the induction heads
items.comment: 4.11 is in the final circuit as a supporting head; 2.2 is missing and the previous-token role is not described.

items.item: Backup name movers take over when name movers are ablated
items.comment: The redundancy was found and measured; 4 of 8 published backup heads are in the circuit.
